rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods <U+2013> factorial randomized block field experiment at Wadi El-Tor, South Sinai, winter 2021, three replicates, two N rates x four drip fertigation schedules plus regular-irrigation control. Q2: Results 'Potato Yield and Yield Components' and Table 4 <U+2013> drip fertigation schedules increased tuber yield by 25.32% and 36.47% with N1 (240 kg N/ha) and N2 (360 kg N/ha) respectively compared with regular irrigation; Table 4 gives treatment means (e.g. N2 control 28.56 vs wise1W 42.76 t/ha). Q4: Table 5 and Fig. 2 <U+2013> total N uptake, N recovery and NUE measured for each treatment and yield shown to be highly correlated with N uptake (R2 0.98/0.96); Fig. 3 <U+2013> soil NO3-N at 0<U+2013>20 and 20<U+2013>40 cm measured, showing fertigation kept more nitrate in the root zone while regular irrigation moved it deeper; LAI at 90 DAP also measured (Table 4).
rows.notes: Single site (one sandy Entisol), one crop/cultivar (Cara), one season <U+2013> no representativeness or scale beyond 3 x 10 m plots. Comparison is drip fertigation vs regular irrigation with soil-applied N, so irrigation method and fertilizer placement/timing are confounded, but this matches the passage wording. Q3 no: only field harvest data, one method. Q7: authors say drip advantages are realised under proper timing and rate of N application, but the yield gain over regular irrigation occurred under all schedules including equal ones, so this is a modifier rather than a stated requirement; treated as no. Q8: no explicit limitation of the yield result stated (only a note that leaching remains possible in sandy soil and that parameters need optimising for other soils/crops). Q9: only LSD letter groupings and an ANOVA CV% (2.61% for tuber yield) in Table 3; no SD/SE/CI for the yield increase itself, so rated no (doubt noted).

notes: Full text appears complete. Minor internal inconsistency: abstract gives 13 and 22% increases of wise weekly over equal schedules; passage figures 25.3/36.4% correspond to Results text 25.32/36.47%.
